hook: SCP-4290 opens with every alarm already ringing: armed task forces, nuclear mines, an orbital strike system, and a sealed entity expected to break loose within a week. Read it as a countdown. It carries the jam-con2019 tag, and it is compact and built toward its final section.
whyItMatters: The file draws on several corners of the wider setting: it quotes SCP-1726 as a source, mentions trips into the Wanderer's Library, and names the Daevites among the ancient cultures that maintained the seal. That makes it a good sampler of the wiki's deep-history worldbuilding. It is also a kaiju-tagged Keter played at full volume.
thingsToNotice:
The dread is built almost entirely from preparation and hearsay: an ancient text in which the Child drinks an island for ten days, TV broadcasts begging viewers to mend its locks, a botched ritual and a deserter's note. The repair rite is grim in a matter-of-fact way, calling for three human corpses and the still-living heart of an angel, and the interrupted attempt takes only two of the bodies and half the heart. Agent Marinos believes the Child now refuses its offerings because they are no longer enough for it, and the file gives you no reason to doubt her yet.

After the file is marked as revised, the payoff lands. The totems crumble, a forty-metre emaciated humanoid surfaces on the lake bed, and the assembled armies wait three hours for it to move before an expedition finds dozens of uneaten corpses and hearts lying on its mouths. The autopsy says it starved to death around 9,000 years ago, so the hunger everyone feared is what killed it, and the seal and its rituals were guarding a corpse for most of their history.
